content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published updated consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis, specifically focusing on rapid diagnostic methods for TB detection. These guidelines, referred to as Module 3: Diagnosis, were updated in 2021 and are available in both electronic and print formats. The electronic version has the ISBN 978-92-4-002941-5, while the print version has the ISBN 978-92-4-002942-2. The guidelines include detailed sections on diagnostic tests for TB, including molecular assays intended as initial tests, low-complexity automated nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) for detecting resistance to isoniazid and second-line anti-TB agents, and high-complexity reverse hybridization-based NAATs for detecting pyrazinamide resistance. The document also provides systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the diagnostic accuracy of these tests. The development of these guidelines involved contributions from a wide range of professionals and experts in TB diagnosis and treatment. Separate Guideline Development Groups (GDGs) were convened for each guideline included in the consolidated document. The acknowledgments section lists the members of these groups, including co-chairs, technical experts, and external reviewers, who contributed their expertise to the development of the recommendations. The funding for the development of these guidelines was provided by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) through a consolidated grant. WHO acknowledges this financial support but clarifies that the funding agency did not influence the content or development of the guidelines. The guidelines also include annexes detailing the methods used for guideline development, conflict of interest assessments for GDG and external review group members, and systematic reviews on the diagnostic accuracy of various TB tests. These annexes provide transparency and ensure the credibility of the recommendations. In summary, the WHO consolidated guidelines on TB diagnosis provide a comprehensive and evidence-based approach to rapid diagnostic methods for TB detection. They are the result of extensive collaboration among global experts and are intended to support healthcare professionals in improving TB diagnosis and treatment outcomes.
